newsitem.title: USA: Chip equipment maker book-to-bill dips in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Chip equipment maker book-to-bill dips in Feb.

text.p: The North American semiconductor manufacturing equipment book-to-bill ratio fell in February to 1.04 from a revised level at 1.08 in January, according to statistics compiled by a trade group.

North American equipment orders fell to $1.1 billion, a 1.5 percent decline from Jan. and 35 percent below Feb. 1995. Shipments rose two percent to $1.05 billion, but were 15 percent under Feb. 1995 levels, Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International reported late on Monday.
A ratio of 1.04 means that for every $104 of orders in the month, $100 of product was shipped during the month.
The ratio, which is based on a three-month moving average, is a general barometer of industry health.
In a statement, the trade group said with a lot of chip fabrication plants coming on-line in 1997, strong equipment orders will likely not return until the second or third quarter of 1997.
